title: Relating a Key-Rank Sample Minimum to Min-Entropy
summary: A sample’s minimum key rank estimates the adversary’s best-case scenario, but its relationship to the key-rank distribution’s min-entropy remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: In side-channel evaluation, the minimum key-rank value observed in a sample from the key-rank distribution estimates the adversary's best-case scenario. Determine whether, and through what relationship, this sample minimum can indicate, estimate, or bound the min-entropy of the key-rank distribution.

scope.domain: Statistical analysis of key-rank distributions in side-channel evaluation.
parameters: Sample minimum key rank: the observed statistic estimating the adversary's best-case scenario
Min-entropy: the target property of the key-rank distribution to be indicated, estimated, or bounded
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether and through what relationship the sample minimum can indicate, estimate, or bound the key-rank distribution's min-entropy.

citations.label: Characterisation and Estimation of the Key Rank Distribution in the Context of Side Channel Evaluations

progress.summary: The paper presents the sample minimum as an estimate of the adversary's best-case scenario and suggests a possible association with min-entropy. It leaves this relationship for future exploration.
citation_labels: Daniel P. Martin et al., Characterisation and Estimation of the Key Rank Distribution in the Context of Side Channel Evaluations
